title: United States reopens its embassy in Kyiv
body:
On 18 May 2022 the United States Department of State announced that it had reopened its embassy in Kyiv. Secretary of State Antony Blinken said in a statement that "the Stars and Stripes are flying over the Embassy once again." He said the United States was taking additional measures to increase the safety of colleagues returning to Kyiv, and he added that "the war rages on."

Washington had pulled out diplomats and suspended operations in Kyiv before the 24 February invasion. On 23 January the United States ordered the families of embassy staff to leave Ukraine, and days before the invasion the remaining staff were moved to Poland. After the reopening, staff returned to Kyiv with tightened security protocols.

President Joe Biden had nominated Bridget Brink, a career foreign service officer who was previously ambassador to Slovakia, as ambassador to Ukraine. She testified at her Senate confirmation hearing on 10 May, and her nomination was still pending before the Senate Foreign Relations Committee at the time of the reopening. The United States had had no Senate-confirmed ambassador in Ukraine since 2019, when President Donald Trump recalled Marie Yovanovitch.
